summary.en: Read and write UTF-8 text with explicit paths, resource ownership and failure handling.
summary.bn: পাথ আর UTF-8 ঠিক করে টেক্সট ফাইল পড়ো-লেখো, I/O সমস্যা সামলাও।

notes: Java 17 supports Files.readString/writeString (since Java 11); every example uses explicit UTF-8.

sections.title: Give data a life beyond one run
Combine a path, charset and operation
Use self-contained files before opening your own
Protect live data during an import
Keep data absence distinct from failure
A successful open is only the beginning

examples.title: Create, read and remove a text file
examples.explanationHtml: A private temporary path avoids assuming a student file already exists. The program prints file contents rather than the varying path.

examples.title: Buffer a line-by-line marks report
examples.explanationHtml: Closing the writer flushes buffered characters before reading begins. readLine returns null at EOF and removes line terminators.

examples.title: Handle an absent file predictably
examples.explanationHtml: The fresh directory guarantees an absent child. A fixed recovery message avoids platform-specific exception path text.

practice.title: Round-trip a line through a file
practice.statementHtml: Read one line of 0..80 printable ASCII characters, possibly empty. Write it to a private temporary UTF-8 file, read it back and print it once with a newline. Delete the temporary file before exit.
hints: Do not trim the input; spaces belong to the line.

practice.title: Sum stored marks line by line
practice.statementHtml: Read n (0..20), followed by n integer marks in 0..100. Write one mark per line to a private temporary UTF-8 file with BufferedWriter. Read using BufferedReader and print the integer sum. Delete the file.
hints: Finish and close writing before opening the reader.

practice.title: Failed imports must not erase valid state
practice.statementHtml: A marks importer clears the current list before reading a file. Halfway through, parsing fails. Repair the update sequence.
practice.answerHtml: Read and validate into a temporary list. Replace the current list only after the entire input succeeds. Catch or propagate IOException and report invalid data separately. The previous valid state then survives a failed import.
hints: Separate preparation from committing a state change.

practice.title: Relative paths and working directories
practice.statementHtml: Why can Path.of("marks.txt") refer to different files when run from an IDE and a terminal?
practice.answerHtml: A relative path is resolved against the process working directory. IDE run configurations and terminal launch folders may differ. Accept a path argument or configure and document the working directory; print a resolved path when diagnosing a real application.
hints: The source folder is not automatically the working directory.

quiz.prompt: Which contents are read after the UTF-8 write completes?
quiz.explanation: writeString stores both lines and readString retrieves their text.

quiz.prompt: What lines does the buffered reader return after the writer closes?
quiz.explanation: Each write is followed by a line separator; readLine strips it before println restores one.

quiz.prompt: How does the absent-file handler affect menu continuation?
quiz.explanation: The catch reports the missing child file and lets normal control continue.

quiz.prompt: Which readLine result means end of file?
quiz.explanation: An empty string can represent a real blank line.
The charset keeps text interpretation consistent across systems.

quiz.prompt: What does Files.newBufferedWriter do by default to an existing file?
quiz.explanation: Use explicit open options when append or exclusive creation is intended.

quiz.prompt: What must happen before another reader relies on buffered writes?
quiz.explanation: Characters may remain in the application buffer until flushed.

quiz.prompt: Which failure family covers many file access errors?
quiz.explanation: Missing files, permission errors and storage failures are I/O failures.

quiz.prompt: When is readString less suitable than streaming lines?
options: For a file too large to hold comfortably in memory
quiz.explanation: readString materializes the whole file as one String.

quiz.prompt: Does an exists check guarantee the next open succeeds?
options: No, the file or permissions may change
quiz.explanation: Attempt the operation and handle its failure; checks cannot eliminate races.

keyPoints.en: A path names a location relative to a filesystem context.
keyPoints.bn: পাথ কোথায় দেখাবে, তা ওয়ার্কিং ডিরেক্টরির ওপরও নির্ভর করে।

keyPoints.en: Specify UTF-8 when a text format requires it.
keyPoints.bn: টেক্সট ফরম্যাটে UTF-8 লাগলে পড়া আর লেখার দুই জায়গায়ই সেটি দাও।

keyPoints.en: readLine distinguishes blank lines from EOF.
keyPoints.bn: readLine খালি লাইনে খালি স্ট্রিং দেয়, ফাইল শেষ হলে null দেয়।

keyPoints.en: Close buffered writers before consuming their files.
keyPoints.bn: লেখা ফাইল পড়ার আগে বাফার্ড রাইটার বন্ধ করো।

keyPoints.en: Validate a complete import before replacing live data.
keyPoints.bn: পুরো ফাইল যাচাই শেষ করে তারপর চলতি ডেটা বদলাও।

examQuestions.question: Describe a safe text marks importer with a temporary result list.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Open a BufferedReader with UTF-8 in try-with-resources. Read until null, validate each line and add parsed marks to a new list. Propagate or report I/O failures. Return or install the new list only after the whole file is valid, preserving the old state on failure.

examQuestions.question: Compare readString and a BufferedReader loop.
examQuestions.answerHtml: readString is concise for small files but stores the entire text. BufferedReader processes one line at a time, enabling bounded working memory when results are not retained. Both need an explicit charset policy and IOException handling.

examQuestions.question: Explain overwrite versus append for a report file.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The default newBufferedWriter options create a missing file or truncate an existing one. To append intentionally, use CREATE and APPEND. Appending still needs record separators, validation and an explicit duplicate-record policy.
